review: The Arabic opens all five stanzas with the same لو (لو لم يحبني), so the Hebrew repeats לוּלֵא with a different title for Christ each time: הַמָּשִׁיחַ, הַסּוֹלֵחַ, הַגִּבּוֹר, הַמְּעֻטָּר.
1:3 הַנִּזְבָּח — 'the Slain One', for الذَّبِيح; זָבַח is the cultic verb and matches the Passover/Lamb charge of the Arabic.
4:2 בַּעֲטֶרֶת סְנֶה — 'with a crown of thornbush'; the Arabic كُلِّلَ بِالْأَشْوَاك is split across the couplet as in the original (الَّذِي / كُلِّلَ).
4:4 בִּשְׁאוֹל הַתַּחְתִּית — 'in lowest Sheol', for فِي وَهْدَةِ الْهَلَاك (in the pit of destruction); the phrase follows Ps 88:7 בְּבוֹר תַּחְתִּיּוֹת.
5:3 לַפּוֹדֶה אֶת־נַפְשִׁי — active participle with a definite object, 'to Him who redeems my soul'; the Hebrew splits the Arabic's relative clause over 5:3–5:4.
